thread:
maya: hitting p95 spikes between GPU nodes during the 09:00 batch window. seeing retransmits + delayed RDMA handshakes. Anyone else?
jorge: yup saw alerts. p95 east-west between rack-a and rack-b up from 3ms to ~70ms for ~2min around 09:02-09:04 :eyes:
ops-oncall: incident-bot: high-eastwest-latency triggered for cluster-gpu-prod (rule: inter-node-p95 > 25ms)
samir: can you paste tcpdump / ethtool output from one of affected hosts?
maya: attaching quick outputs (snips). run on gpu-node-12:
[code]
# ethtool -k eth0
rx-checksumming: on
tx-checksumming: on
gro: on
gso: on
# ip link show eth0
eth0: mtu 9000 qlen 1000
[/code]
maya: tcpdump shows lots of MSS=1440 fragments and occasional retransmit markers during the spike
li: wait mtu 9000 on node-12 but our switch logs show PMTU negotiated 1500 for ports in rack-b a-minute earlier
jorge: aha - maybe a partial jumbo enablement during last-week rolling upgrade. some hosts ended up with 9000, others with 1500 -> fragmentation + RDMA fallback
samir: that would explain bursts only under high batch concurrency (large RDMA writes + KV cache syncs). RDMA will fallback to UDP/TCP path causing latency.
maya: quick mitigation: set ip link mtu 1500 on node-12 and node-14 in rack-a, rolling in affected racks. will that break other services?
li: note: Dedicated capacity nodes in rack-c rely on 9000 for throughput. reducing to 1500 increases CPU/network overhead. need approval from product for short perf hit
ops-oncall: can we do a targeted route-shift instead? route GPU batching traffic via rack-c temporarily?
jorge: routing is messy during peak. simpler/faster to align MTU on the small set of misconfigured hosts. created playbook: ansible change -> if qlen+restarts stable, mark as fixed.
maya: ran quick iperf between node-12 and node-20 pre/post mtu change:
[code]
iperf3 -c node-20
before: 2.3 Gbits/sec (lots of retransmits)
after: 9.6 Gbits/sec (clean)
[/code]
samir: good. can we add a fleet check to detect MTU drift? grep config vs switch? maybe use LLDP + config audit
li: added ticket INFRA-2456 to run daily MTU audit + RDMA health check (owners: samir, jorge). link: https://tracker/redwood/INFRA-2456
ops-oncall: temporary mitigation: rollback the last jumbo frame flag PR to avoid wider drift. PR #789
maya: marking postmortem needed if this recurs. will collect packet captures and compile quick runbook.
infra-bot: deploy-bot: playbook run started on 6 hosts (change: set mtu=1500) — ETA 4m
maya: thanks all. will update once finished :thumbsup:
